 UVA Health buys former State Farm building on Pantops to expand outpatient care 
 UVA HEALTH (WVIR) By Emma Grace Myers Published : Oct. 30, 2026 at 2:56 PM EDT | Updated : 11 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google ALBEMARLE COUNTY, Va. (WVIR) - Big changes are coming to the old State Farm building on Pantops.
 UVA Health announced Friday that it has bought the 55-acre property for a net price of $37.7 million, with plans to turn the 365,000-square-foot facility into a major outpatient center by 2028.
 State Farm cleared out of the complex at 1500 State Farm Boulevard in 2020 after shifting staff to remote work. Being near both U.S 250 and Interstate 64 makes it a convenient, accessible hub for patients across Central Virginia.
 The purchase is part of UVA Health’s 10-year space plan initiative, Expanding Care, Enhancing Lives, which aims to keep up with surging demand. Mitchell Rosner, chief executive officer of UVA Health and executive vice president for health affairs at UVA, said they expect outpatient visits in the Charlottesville area to climb to 1.2 million a year by 2035, about 300,000 more than they handle right now.
 Shifting more routine appointments and specialty clinics out to Pantops also solves another big headache: crowding at the main hospital. Over the next six months they will determine which clinical services are best suited for this location and what renovations will need to be done. 
 Work is also currently underway at the University Hospital, which operated at 91% capacity in the 2026 fiscal year. Crews are currently finishing the top three floors of the South Tower to add beds for cancer patients, pediatrics, and the NICU. UVA is also converting its Transitional Care Hospital on Ivy Road into behavioral health rooms. Combined, the moves will free up 137 more inpatient beds at the main hospital over the next three years.
